verdict.topBlocker: Customer organizations have OAuth app access restrictions on by default, so an org owner must approve your app before the agent can reach that org's private repositories; this is customer-side, not a GitHub review.
verdict.summary: Required wait: none; any GitHub user can authorize a registered OAuth app immediately, with no GitHub review, verification or distribution switch. Optional: Marketplace listing and publisher verification (needed only for paid plans or a badge; no official timeline). Limits: each customer org owner must approve the app for private org data, tokens share the user's 5,000 req/hour budget (15,000 for Enterprise Cloud orgs), and 10 tokens per user/app/scope.
verdict.reason: Numeric verdict confirmed (no provider gate, so 0-0 days and difficulty 2 stand). Summary reworded to keep the community 2-6 week Marketplace figure out of the verdict and to separate required wait, optional listings and post-connect limits; rate-limit claim corrected to include the 15,000/hour Enterprise Cloud tier.

optionalPaths.name: GitHub Marketplace free listing (onboarding-expert review)
optionalPaths.why: For vendors wanting discovery inside GitHub; not needed for OAuth to work. Official docs give no timeline; a community source (devactivity.com) reports roughly 2-6 weeks.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/apps/github-marketplace/listing-an-app-on-github-marketplace/submitting-your-listing-for-publication "you can request a review by an onboarding expert"

optionalPaths.name: Publisher verification for the owning organization
optionalPaths.why: Only for vendors who want paid Marketplace plans or a Marketplace badge; requires org-owned app, org 2FA, verified domain and support email.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/apps/github-marketplace/github-marketplace-overview/applying-for-publisher-verification-for-your-organization "To offer paid plans for your app or to include a marketplace badge"

optionalPaths.name: Paid GitHub Marketplace listing
optionalPaths.why: Only for vendors billing through GitHub; needs verified publisher, purchase-event handling, monthly and annual billing, and should have 200+ users for an OAuth app.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/apps/github-marketplace/creating-apps-for-github-marketplace/requirements-for-listing-an-app "OAuth apps should have a minimum of 200 users."

limits.limit: Org OAuth app access restrictions (on by default for new orgs)
limits.impact: The agent sees only public data and the user's own repos until each customer org owner grants access, so onboarding org customers needs an admin step per org; a Marketplace listing does not bypass this.
limits.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-oauth-access-to-your-organizations-data/about-oauth-app-access-restrictions "API access to private organization resources is not available for unapproved OAuth apps."

limits.limit: User rate limit 5,000 requests/hour (15,000 for Enterprise Cloud orgs), shared with the user's other apps and PATs, plus secondary limits
limits.impact: A busy agent can exhaust a user's hourly budget and break the user's other tools; heavy workloads point toward a GitHub App, not toward a listing.
limits.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api "All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour."

limits.limit: Ten tokens per user/application/scope; ten token creations per hour
limits.impact: An agent that mints a fresh token per session or worker will silently revoke older tokens, so store and reuse one token per user/scope set.
limits.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/authorizing-oauth-apps "There is a limit of ten tokens that are issued per user/application/scope combination"

limits.limit: Expiring tokens: 8-hour access token, refresh token valid 6 months without use (on by default)
limits.impact: Long-running agents must implement refresh, and a user idle for 6 months must reconnect.
limits.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/authorizing-oauth-apps "The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use."

limits.limit: Device flow: 50 code submissions/hour per app; user code valid 15 minutes
limits.impact: Headless/CLI agent sign-ins across many users can hit the per-app hourly cap; use web flow for scale.
limits.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/authorizing-oauth-apps "there is a rate limit of 50 submissions in an hour per application"

limits.limit: No connected-user or install cap for unlisted OAuth apps
limits.impact: Nothing in the docs caps users of an unlisted app, so no limit makes a Marketplace listing practically necessary for an AI agent.
limits.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/creating-an-oauth-app documents only "A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps." (no user cap)

stepChanges.newDetail: Generate a client secret on the app's settings page and keep it only in your backend (environment variable or secret store). Never ship it in browser or mobile code; do the code exchange server-side.
stepChanges.reason: Linked source is a community discussion, not official docs; detail kept but should not be presented as GitHub-sourced.

stepChanges.newDetail: Redirect to https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri (must exactly match a registered callback unless wildcard matching is enabled), scope and an unguessable state. PKCE is optional but recommended: send code_challenge (43-char SHA-256) with code_challenge_method=S256; plain is not supported.
stepChanges.reason: Original implied PKCE is part of the required request and omitted S256-only and redirect matching rules.

stepChanges.newDetail: Put the Client ID and server-side Client Secret in production config. Any GitHub user can connect immediately with no GitHub review, but for customer organizations with OAuth app access restrictions (default on) an org owner must approve the app before the agent can reach private org repositories.
stepChanges.reason: 'Without waiting for platform approval' is true for GitHub but hides the default-on org-owner approval that blocks private org data.

stepChanges.newTitle: (Optional) Publisher Verification for paid Marketplace plans or badge
stepChanges.newDetail: Only needed to offer paid Marketplace plans or show a Marketplace badge. Transfer the app to an organization, enable org 2FA, verify a domain, set a support email, then request verification. GitHub states no timeline.
stepChanges.reason: Original framed verification as needed for any Marketplace listing; docs tie it to paid plans or the badge.
Already optional; keep the 2-6 week figure explicitly labelled community, official docs give no timeline.

missing: Requests from apps owned or approved by a GitHub Enterprise Cloud org get 15,000 requests/hour, and the 5,000/hour user limit is shared with the user's PATs and other authorized apps. https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api

Creating more than ten tokens for the same user/app/scope revokes an existing token, so per-session token minting breaks earlier sessions. https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/authorizing-oauth-apps

Orgs using SAML SSO require the user to have an active SSO session so a credential authorization is attached to the token for that org; otherwise org resources are unreachable. https://docs.github.com/en/apps/using-github-apps/saml-and-github-apps

OAuth app scopes are coarse (repo grants full read/write to all public and private repos); GitHub Apps offer fine-grained, per-repository permissions and are GitHub's general recommendation. https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/differences-between-github-apps-and-oauth-apps
Secondary rate limits (e.g. max 100 concurrent requests, content-creation limits) apply and can change without notice. https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api
